title: Prefix sums and difference arrays
lead: Essential; the two-dimensional prefix sums and differences are Advanced. Running totals for range-sum queries, and their inverse, differences, for range updates. The text counts from 1, with a0 = S0 = 0 (its Convention box); the code counts from 0. TheAlgorithms’ PrefixSum treats a range starting at 0 apart, and the doocs code pads its table with a zero row and column, so s[i + 1][j + 1] is Si+1, j+1, and writes d[r + 1].
notes: OI Wiki’s code, its Luogu P1387 example and its sections on subset sums and on trees are not included here.
exercise_notes: No exercise with a printed statement and tests poses a prefix-sum or difference-array problem yet. TheAlgorithms’ PrefixSum and equilibrium-index doctests and keon’s sum_sub_squares tests are tests with no statement of their own; the Kattis problems sumoftheothers, commercials, shortsell, pivot and freefood come with sample data only; and Kattis subseqhard, which needs a hash map, is held for chapter 5.
